name: Game of Stacks
description: You have $$$n$$$ stacks $$$r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_n$$$. Each stack contains some positive integers ranging from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Define the following functions: function init(pos): stacks := an array that contains n stacks r[1], r[2], ..., r[n] return get(stacks, pos) function get(stacks, pos): if stacks[pos] is empty: return pos else: new_pos := the top element of stacks[pos] pop the top element of stacks[pos] return get(stacks, new_pos) You want to know the values returned by $$$\texttt{init(1)}, \texttt{init(2)}, \ldots, \texttt{init(n)}$$$. Note that, during these calls, the stacks $$$r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_n$$$ don't change, so the calls $$$\texttt{init(1)}, \texttt{init(2)}, \ldots, \texttt{init(n)}$$$ are independent.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1\le n\le 10^5$$$) — the length of the array $$$r$$$. Each of the following $$$n$$$ lines contains several integers. The first integer $$$k_i$$$ ($$$0\le k_i\le 10^5$$$) represents the number of elements in the $$$i$$$-th stack, and the following $$$k_i$$$ positive integers $$$c_{i,1},c_{i,2},\ldots,c_{i,k_i}$$$ ($$$1\le c_{i,j}\le n$$$) represent the elements in the $$$i$$$-th stack. $$$c_{i,1}$$$ is the bottom element. In each test, $$$\sum k_i\le 10^6$$$.
output_specification: You need to output $$$n$$$ values, the $$$i$$$-th of which is the value returned by $$$\texttt{init(i)}$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1889D — Game of Stacks [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
